source.title: Mapping Class Group Factorizations and Symplectic 4-Manifolds: Some Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let Map_g be the mapping class group of a closed genus-g surface and Map_{g,n} the mapping class group of a genus-g surface with n boundary components. A mapping class group factorization is an ordered product of positive Dehn twists, typically a factorization of the identity in Map_g or of the boundary twist delta in Map_{g,n}. Two such factorizations are compared using Hurwitz moves, meaning the braid-group moves on adjacent Dehn-twist factors, and global conjugation, meaning simultaneous conjugation of all factors by one mapping class. Is the Hurwitz problem for mapping class group factorizations decidable, and are there useful criteria for proving that two given factorizations are equivalent or inequivalent under Hurwitz moves and global conjugation?

View a Lefschetz fibration with genus-g fibers as a smooth map phi from S^2 to the compactified moduli space of genus-g curves, where singular fibers correspond to positive transverse intersections with the divisor of nodal curves. Can one find special geometric representatives for such maps, for example trees of conformal harmonic maps, and use those representatives to decompose or understand Lefschetz fibrations in terms of holomorphic pieces?

Given a Lefschetz fibration f and its monodromy factorization by positive Dehn twists, can one enumerate all matching paths? A matching path is an embedded arc in S^2 minus the critical values of f, with endpoints at critical values, such that parallel transport along the arc sends the two endpoint vanishing cycles to mutually homotopic loops in the fiber.

For a Lefschetz fibration f with total space M, and for the corresponding blown-down symplectic 4-manifold X when distinguished sections are used, which homology classes in H_2(M,Z) or H_2(X,Z) can be represented by Lagrangian spheres that arise from matching paths?

For a Lefschetz fibration whose monodromy factorization is an ordered tuple of Dehn twists, an automorphism of the fibration is a braid acting by Hurwitz moves that carries the tuple to a globally conjugate tuple. Can one find generators for this automorphism group, together with a collection of matching paths, such that every matching path is obtained from one of the chosen paths by applying an automorphism of the fibration?

Let Map_{g,n} be the mapping class group of a genus-g surface with n greater than 0 boundary components, and let delta be the boundary twist, the product of positive Dehn twists parallel to the boundary components. Under the relative-minimality assumption that every component of every reducible singular fiber intersects at least one distinguished section, is there an a priori upper bound on the length of any factorization of delta as a product of positive Dehn twists in Map_{g,n}? Equivalently, is there a genus-only upper bound on the number of singular fibers of a Lefschetz fibration admitting a section of square -1?

Let Map^+_{g,n} be the sub-semigroup of Map_{g,n} generated by positive Dehn twists. For which elements T in Map^+_{g,n} can factorizations of T as products of positive Dehn twists be classified in Map_{g,n}; in particular, for which T is the factorization unique, or finite in number, up to Hurwitz equivalence and global conjugation? Geometrically, such factorizations correspond to Lefschetz fibrations over a disk with boundary monodromy T and to Stein fillings of the contact 3-manifold carried by the corresponding open book.

Let delta be the boundary twist in Map_{g,n}. Given two factorizations of delta as products of positive Dehn twists along nonseparating curves in Map_{g,n}, suppose the total spaces of the corresponding Lefschetz fibrations have the same Euler characteristic and signature. Is it always possible to transform one factorization into the other by a sequence of Hurwitz moves and partial conjugations, where a partial conjugation conjugates a contiguous block of factors by a Dehn twist that commutes with the product of that block? Equivalently at the symplectic 4-manifold level, are compact integral symplectic 4-manifolds with the same c_1^2, c_2, [omega]^2, and c_1 dot [omega] related by Luttinger surgeries?

For compact symplectic 6-manifolds, after blowing up finitely many points so that the manifold can be viewed as a singular fibration over CP^2 whose singular locus is a symplectic curve with cusp and node singularities, can representations of fundamental groups of plane-curve complements into mapping class groups be studied in a way that improves understanding of the topology of symplectic 6-manifolds, analogous to the role of mapping class group factorizations for symplectic 4-manifolds?

trace.notes: Normalized the input as a zbMATH resolver URL with document id 5124680. Local resolver metadata in outputs/open-problems-0418-all.csv identifies the title as Mapping class group factorizations and symplectic 4-manifolds: some open problems.

The live zbMATH resolver page was not readable in the available fetch environment, and local shell fetching failed because DNS resolution is unavailable in the sandbox. Exact-title recovery found an author-hosted PDF whose visible title and author match the zbMATH record, so that PDF was used as the readable primary source.

Mapped the PDF as an 11-page article. Section 1 defines Lefschetz fibrations, monodromy, positive Dehn twists, mapping class group factorizations, Hurwitz equivalence, global conjugation, boundary twists, and the connection with symplectic 4-manifolds. Section 2 contains the labeled questions and related open directions.
Extracted the five labeled questions, the Tian-related question, two matching-path refinements, and the closing symplectic-6-manifold representation direction.
Expanded the Hurwitz problem by inlining the meanings of Map_g, Map_{g,n}, positive Dehn-twist factorizations, Hurwitz moves, and global conjugation from Section 1.
Rewrote the Tian-related question using the preceding description of Lefschetz fibrations as maps to compactified moduli space.
Expanded Donaldson's matching-path question by including the source definition of matching path.
Separated the homology-class variant from the matching-path enumeration question because it asks for representable classes rather than enumeration of paths.
Expanded the automorphism-group variant by inlining the source definition of automorphism as a braid stabilizing the monodromy factorization up to global conjugation.
Expanded Smith's boundary-twist length question by including the relative-minimality assumption and the Lefschetz-fibration equivalent formulation.
Expanded the classification question for T in Map^+_{g,n} by including the Stein-filling interpretation stated immediately before the question.
Expanded the partial-conjugation question by including the stated condition on Euler characteristic and signature and the Luttinger-surgery analogue.
Converted the closing research direction about symplectic 6-manifolds into a self-contained question while preserving the stated singular-fibration setup.
No near-duplicates were merged. The matching-path enumeration, homology-class, and automorphism-group candidates were kept separate because they ask for different outputs.
All accepted items include self-contained rewritten question text, solved-status metadata set to false, and page-located source evidence. No item was marked solved in the source.
Saved final JSON to outputs/parse-paper/5124680.json and outputs/latest.json.
